CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.SECTION_HELP_PAM_POLICY: Leave a field empty to use the platform's setting.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_PASSWORD_POLICY: The rules of this connection's new passwords, in place of its platform's, for a host with its own requirements. Policies are set on the Password Policies tab.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_SSH_PORT: Empty: the SSH connection's port, or else the platform's.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_SSH_HOST_KEY: SHA256 fingerprint of the host key, as ssh-keygen -l prints it. Empty: the platform's SSH CA keys decide; without any, the host is refused, its key shown in the error to check and pin here, unless the platform trusts new host keys.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL: Empty: the connection's username, in the platform's realm.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_DATABASE_ACCOUNT_HOST: The host part of the account, as in 'name'@'host'. Empty: %. Other databases ignore it.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_WINRM_CERTIFICATE: SHA-256 fingerprint of the host's certificate. Empty: the platform's CA certificates decide; without any, the host is refused, its certificate shown in the error to check and pin here, unless the platform trusts new certificates.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_CHECKOUT_EXCLUSIVE: Only one holder at a time:
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_CHECKOUT_EXCLUSIVE: Whether a checkout keeps others from checking out the connection until it ends. Automatic: yes when a platform manages the password, as it changes once the holder is done; no when it is only stored.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_APPROVALS_REQUIRED: How many distinct approvers must approve each request. Empty: none.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_EXTENSIONS: Whether holders may extend their access, with the same approvals as a request, and ask for several time limits at once. Default: as on the PAM Settings tab, yes unless changed.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HELP_PAM_MAX_EXTENSIONS: Per checkout, counting time limits asked for at once beyond the first. Empty: as on the PAM Settings tab, 2 unless changed.
CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES.FIELD_HEADER_PAM_REVEAL_PASSWORD: Let users holding access see the password:

PAM.HELP_BADGES: Counts shown next to your name and on their settings tab, so you notice what needs your attention. Turning a badge off only hides the count; the tabs still list everything.
PAM.HELP_CHECKOUTS: Passwords and connection access currently held by users. Revoking a checkout ends it immediately, closes the holder's open sessions on that connection, and rotates the password if it is managed to rotate after each use.
PAM.HELP_CONNECTIONS: Connections assigned to a platform (set up on the Platforms tab). Rotation logs in to the target with the stored credentials, changes the password as the platform describes, and stores the new password only after the target accepts it.
PAM.HELP_HOST_KEY: Key trusted for this target: pinned, recorded at the first contact (if its platform trusts new keys), or the one that last passed the check. Rotation refuses a different key until the new one is pasted into the connection's "Trusted SSH host key" field.
PAM.HELP_PLATFORMS: Platforms describe how passwords of a group of systems are changed, and when. A connection is managed once it is assigned a platform in its "Password management" settings.
PAM.HELP_ROTATE_ALL: Rotate the passwords of every connection listed, as filtered, a few at a time
PAM.HELP_STORED_SECRETS: Passwords of this platform are stored, shown masked. Leave them as they are to keep them, unless you change where they are sent (server, port, encryption, trusted certificate or CA certificates): enter them again then. Clear one to remove it.
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_CASE: Wait until the output since the last send matches the regular expression of one of the cases, run the lines of the case matching first in the output, then continue after @end. Cases cannot hold other cases
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_FAIL: End the script, reporting this text as the problem, such as in a case matching an error
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_COMMENT: Comment, ignored, as are empty lines
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_ESCAPE: Send a line starting with @ or # as-is
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_EXPECT: Wait until the output since the last send contains this text
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_REGEX: Wait until the output since the last send matches this regular expression
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_SEND: Any other line is sent exactly as typed (spaces included), followed by Enter
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_SEND_EMPTY: Press Enter (or "@send text" to send text)
PAM.HELP_SYNTAX_TIMEOUT: Seconds each following expect may wait (default 10)
PAM.HELP_TEST_PLATFORM: Check the settings as they are, without saving them or changing any password: the server is reached and trusted, and the rotation account, if any, signs in
PAM.HELP_TYPE_DATABASE: PostgreSQL roles, MySQL and MariaDB accounts, and SQL Server logins, for Account connections whose holders use the password in their own client. Changes passwords as an administrator account or as the account itself, over TLS. Uses the database's JDBC driver installed in GUACAMOLE_HOME/lib.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_KERBEROS: MIT Kerberos, Heimdal and Active Directory domains, over kpasswd (RFC 3244). Changes principal passwords as an admin principal or as the principal itself.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_WINRM: Local Windows accounts only, over HTTPS only. Sets their passwords as an administrator or as the account itself (which must then be an administrator); for domain accounts, use LDAP or Kerberos. Host certificates are checked against your CA's certificates, or pinned on each connection.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_LDAP: OpenLDAP, Active Directory and other directories, over LDAPS or StartTLS. Changes account passwords as an administrator or as the account itself. Active Directory requires encryption.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_TACACS: Accounts held by a TACACS+ server itself, over its password change dialogue (RFC 8907), with the account's current password. Only where the server allows password changes, such as tac_plus-ng with a backend storing passwords: a server says so only when asked to change one. For accounts the server checks in a directory, use LDAP or Kerberos.
PAM.HELP_TYPE_SSH: Any system reachable over SSH: a send/expect script changes the password, such as passwd on Linux or net user on Windows (OpenSSH). The host key is pinned on the connection, certified by your SSH CA, or trusted on first contact if the platform allows it.
PAM.INFO_ACTIVE_SESSIONS: {COUNT, plural, one{1 active session} other{# active sessions}}
PAM.INFO_BADGE_FAILURES: {COUNT, plural, one{1 managed connection needs} other{# managed connections need}} attention: the last rotation failed or could not be confirmed
PAM.INFO_NO_CONNECTIONS: No connection is assigned to a platform yet.
PAM.INFO_PLATFORM_CONNECTIONS: {COUNT, plural, =0{No connections} one{1 connection} other{# connections}}
PAM.TEXT_CONFIRM_DELETE_PLATFORM: Delete the platform "{NAME}"? This cannot be undone.
PAM.TEXT_CONFIRM_REVOKE_CHECKOUT: End the checkout of "{NAME}" by {USER} now?
PAM.TEXT_CONFIRM_ROTATE_ALL: Rotate the passwords of {COUNT, plural, one{the managed connection} other{the # managed connections}} now?
PAM.TEXT_CONFIRM_ROTATE_FILTERED: Rotate the passwords of {COUNT, plural, one{the connection} other{the # connections}} matching the filter now? Connections the filter hides are left as they are.
PAM.TEXT_DISCARD_CHANGES: Discard unsaved changes to this platform?
PAM.TEXT_ROTATE_ALL_REQUEST_FAILED: {COUNT, plural, one{1 rotation} other{# rotations}} could not be started; see the list for the status of each connection.

HOME.HELP_MANAGE: Open the request (to release it, or cancel it)

REQUEST.ACCESS_HELP_PASSWORD: You may see this connection's password. Each time you do is recorded.
REQUEST.ACCESS_HELP_PASSWORD_MANAGED: You may see this connection's password. Each time you do is recorded, and the password is changed once your access ends.
REQUEST.ACCESS_HELP_PENDING: Once approved, you have access for {MINUTES} minutes. Open this connection again to connect.
REQUEST.ACCESS_HELP_PENDING_LATER: Once approved, you have access at that time. Open this connection again then to connect.
REQUEST.ACCESS_HELP_RELEASE: Release access when you are done. Open sessions end when access ends.
REQUEST.ACCESS_HELP_RELEASE_MANAGED: Release access as soon as you are done, so its password can be changed. Open sessions end when access ends.
REQUEST.ACCESS_HELP_RESERVED: Open this connection again then to connect.
REQUEST.ACCESS_TEXT_AVAILABLE: This connection needs a request. You will have access for {MINUTES} minutes.
REQUEST.ACCESS_TEXT_AVAILABLE_EXCLUSIVE: This connection needs a request. You will have access, alone, for {MINUTES} minutes.
REQUEST.ACCESS_TEXT_HELD: You have access to this connection. Time remaining: {REMAINING}
REQUEST.ACCESS_TEXT_RESERVATION_STARTED: Your approved access is ready, until {ENDS}.
REQUEST.ACCESS_TEXT_RESERVED: Approved: you have access from {STARTS} to {ENDS}.
REQUEST.ACCESS_TEXT_NEEDS_APPROVAL: Access to this connection needs {REQUIRED, plural, one{1 approval} other{# approvals}}. Once approved, you have access for {MINUTES} minutes.
REQUEST.HELP_DURATION: Longer than the time limit uses up extensions: {LEFT, plural, =0{none will be left} one{1 will be left} other{# will be left}}.
REQUEST.HELP_EXTEND: You can extend this by {TOTAL}, {LEFT, plural, one{once more} other{# more times}}{REQUIRED, plural, =0{} one{, with 1 approval} other{, with # approvals}}.
REQUEST.HELP_PENDING: Once approved, the password is checked out to you for {MINUTES} minutes. Open this account again to see it.
REQUEST.HELP_PENDING_LATER: Once approved, the password is yours at that time. Open this account again then to see it.
REQUEST.HELP_RELEASE: Release the password when you are done.
REQUEST.HELP_RELEASE_MANAGED: Release the password as soon as you are done, so it can be changed.
REQUEST.HELP_RESERVED: Open this account again then to see the password.
REQUEST.INFO_RESERVED_BY_OTHER: Reserved by {USER} from {STARTS} to {ENDS}. Access taken before then ends when that starts.
REQUEST.TEXT_AVAILABLE: The password will be checked out to you for {MINUTES} minutes and then released automatically.
REQUEST.TEXT_AVAILABLE_EXCLUSIVE: The password will be checked out to you alone for {MINUTES} minutes and then released automatically.
REQUEST.TEXT_EXPIRED: The checkout has expired and the password was released.
REQUEST.TEXT_EXTENSION_DENIED: Your last extension was denied by {USER}.
REQUEST.TEXT_HELD: You hold this password. Time remaining: {REMAINING}
REQUEST.TEXT_HELD_BY_OTHER: This password is checked out by {USER} until {EXPIRES}.
REQUEST.TEXT_LAST_DENIED: Your last request was denied by {USER}.
REQUEST.TEXT_LAST_EXPIRED: Your last request expired before it was approved.
REQUEST.TEXT_LAST_REJECTED: Your last request was rejected automatically.
REQUEST.TEXT_NEEDS_APPROVAL: This password needs {REQUIRED, plural, one{1 approval} other{# approvals}}. Once approved, it is checked out to you for {MINUTES} minutes.
REQUEST.TEXT_RESERVATION_STARTED: Your approved checkout is ready, until {ENDS}.
REQUEST.TEXT_RESERVED: Approved: the password is yours from {STARTS} to {ENDS}.

PAM_TYPE_SSH.FIELD_HELP_PORT: Used when a connection gives no SSH port. Empty: 22.
PAM_TYPE_SSH.FIELD_HELP_SSH_CA_KEYS: Public keys of the certificate authorities that sign your hosts' SSH host certificates, one per line, as in the CA's .pub file. A host presenting a certificate one of them signed, naming the host and valid now, is trusted without a pinned key. Empty: host keys are pinned on each connection.
PAM_TYPE_SSH.FIELD_HELP_TRUST_FIRST_KEY: Without SSH CA keys, accept the key a host presents at the first contact, when its connection pins none, and require it from then on, as ssh does with known_hosts. Unchecked: such a host is refused until its key is pinned on the connection.

PAM_TYPE_LDAP.FIELD_HELP_LDAP_CERTIFICATE_FINGERPRINT: SHA-256 fingerprint of the server's certificate, as openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256 prints it. Empty: the certificate must be issued by a CA Java trusts.
PAM_TYPE_LDAP.FIELD_HELP_LDAP_ADMIN_DN: Empty: each account changes its own password.
PAM_TYPE_LDAP.FIELD_HELP_LDAP_SHOW_DN: Whether users checking out an account see its DN beside its username. Unchecked: the username only.

PAM_TYPE_KERBEROS.FIELD_HELP_KERBEROS_REALM: Usually upper case, such as EXAMPLE.ORG.
PAM_TYPE_KERBEROS.FIELD_HELP_KERBEROS_KPASSWD_SERVER: The password change server. Empty: the KDC.
PAM_TYPE_KERBEROS.FIELD_HELP_KERBEROS_KPASSWD_PORT: Port of the password change server. Empty: 464.
PAM_TYPE_KERBEROS.FIELD_HELP_KERBEROS_ADMIN_PRINCIPAL: Empty: each principal changes its own password.

PAM_TYPE_WINRM.FIELD_HELP_WINRM_ADMIN_USERNAME: Empty: each account sets its own password.
PAM_TYPE_WINRM.FIELD_HELP_WINRM_CA_CERTIFICATES: Set: hosts' certificates must be issued by one of these and name the host. Empty: each host's certificate must be pinned on its connection, unless new certificates are trusted.
PAM_TYPE_WINRM.FIELD_HELP_WINRM_TRUST_FIRST_CERTIFICATE: Without CA certificates, accept the certificate a host presents at the first contact, when its connection pins none, and require it from then on. Unchecked: such a host is refused until its certificate is pinned on the connection.

PAM_TYPE_DATABASE.FIELD_HELP_DATABASE_NAME: Where to connect, for servers allowing accounts only some databases. Empty: postgres (PostgreSQL), master (SQL Server), none (MySQL, MariaDB). Letters, digits, _, $ and - only.
PAM_TYPE_DATABASE.FIELD_HELP_DATABASE_CA_CERTIFICATES: Certificates of the CAs issuing the server's certificate, or the server's own certificate. Empty: the CAs Java trusts. The certificate must name the server's hostname either way.
PAM_TYPE_DATABASE.FIELD_HELP_DATABASE_ADMIN_USERNAME: Empty: each account changes its own password. It needs CREATEROLE and the ADMIN option on each role (PostgreSQL), CREATE USER (MySQL, MariaDB), or ALTER ANY LOGIN, and CONTROL SERVER for sysadmin logins (SQL Server).

PAM_TYPE_TACACS.FIELD_HELP_TACACS_BACKUP_SERVER: Tried when the server cannot be reached, on the same port with the same shared secret. Empty: none.
PAM_TYPE_TACACS.FIELD_HELP_TACACS_SECRET: The key the server shares with this Guacamole server, which must also be allowed as a client.

PAM_POLICY.FIELD_HELP_PASSWORD_POLICY: The rules of new passwords, as the platform's systems require: set on the Password Policies tab. Default: 24 characters of every kind.

PAM_HISTORY.HELP_HISTORY: Every checkout of a password or of access to a connection, active or ended, newest first. Search matches the user, account, reason, how and by whom a checkout ended, who approved it, or the address of any of them. Click a user, approver or who ended a checkout for when and from where they did so. Click a reason to read it in full, or a column header to sort.
PAM_HISTORY.HELP_SHOW_APPROVALS: Show who approved, when, and from where
PAM_HISTORY.HELP_SHOW_ENDED: Show who ended it, when, and from where
PAM_HISTORY.HELP_SHOW_EXTENSIONS: Show each extension: when, by how much, why, and who approved it
PAM_HISTORY.HELP_SHOW_HOLDER: Show when and from where it was checked out
PAM_HISTORY.TEXT_EXTENSIONS_LEFT: {USED} of {MAX, plural, one{1 extension} other{# extensions}} allowed used.

PAM_APPROVALS.HELP_HISTORY: Every decided request you may see, newest first: approved, denied, cancelled by its requester, or expired. Search matches the requester, connection, account, reason, decision, who decided, the reason for a denial, or the address of anyone who requested or decided. Click a requester, approver or scheduled access for its details. Click a reason to read it in full, or a column header to sort.
PAM_APPROVALS.FIELD_DENY_REASON: Reason for the denial (shown to the requester):
PAM_APPROVALS.HELP_SHOW_ACCESS: Show when the access starts and ends, and for how long
PAM_APPROVALS.HELP_SHOW_DECISION: Show who decided, when, and from where
PAM_APPROVALS.HELP_SHOW_REQUESTER: Show when and from where it was requested
PAM_APPROVALS.HELP_PENDING: Requests awaiting approval that you may decide on: those of the connections your approval permission (or that of one of your groups) covers. Administrators see all. A request needs as many distinct approvers as its connection requires; one denial rejects it. Once approved, the requester's checkout starts, or, for a request ahead of time, the connection is theirs at that time. Requests left pending for 24 hours expire, and those ahead of time once their time is over. Approving one ahead of time rejects the others awaiting approval for an overlapping time, where the connection is held by one user at a time.
PAM_APPROVALS.INFO_BADGE: {COUNT, plural, one{1 request awaits} other{# requests await}} your approval

PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_APPROVE_CONNECTION: May approve requests for this connection
PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_APPROVE_GROUP: May approve requests for every connection in this group, including ones added later
PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_SELECT_GROUP: Members may approve requests for the connections and connection groups ticked "Approve" in the connections list below.
PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.HELP_SELECT_USER: This user may approve requests for the connections and connection groups ticked "Approve" in the connections list below.
PAM_APPROVAL_PERMISSIONS.INFO_SELECTED: {COUNT, plural, =0{Tick "Approve" in the connections list below} one{1 ticked "Approve" below} other{# ticked "Approve" below}}

PAM_PASSWORD_POLICIES.FIELD_HEADER_EXCLUDE_AMBIGUOUS: Leave out characters easily mistaken for others (l, I, O, 0, 1)
PAM_PASSWORD_POLICIES.HELP_DEFAULT: The rules of platforms and connections choosing no policy. It cannot be changed: create a policy, and choose it, to make passwords another way.
PAM_PASSWORD_POLICIES.HELP_POLICIES: Rules of the passwords generated when rotating, for target systems with their own requirements. A platform chooses a policy in its rotation policy, and a connection may choose another. Without one, the default applies.
PAM_PASSWORD_POLICIES.TEXT_CONFIRM_DELETE: Delete the password policy "{NAME}"? A policy still used by a platform or connection cannot be deleted.
PAM_PASSWORD_POLICIES.TEXT_SHELL_SPECIAL: These symbols have a meaning on command lines: {SYMBOLS}. Passwords containing them break SSH scripts that type the password into a command, rather than at a prompt. Leave them out for such platforms.

PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_ADMIN_BYPASS_REQUESTS: Administrators connect to connections, and check out Accounts, without a request, which is logged. Otherwise they skip approvals only, and give a reason like anyone else.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_EXTENSIONS_ENABLED: Whether holders may extend their checkouts, for connections leaving it to this setting.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_MAX_EXTENSIONS: How many times a checkout may be extended, for connections leaving it to this setting. Requests may also ask for up to one more than this many time limits at once.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SHARED: Shared by every Guacamole server using this database, and applied to all of them within seconds, without a restart. Connections can override some of them.
PAM_SETTINGS.STANDBY_STARTING: PAM is starting on this Guacamole server.
PAM_SETTINGS.STANDBY_OTHER_SERVER: Another Guacamole server runs PAM on this database without the HA module, so this one is on standby until that one stops. PAM is read-only here: no checkouts, approvals, rotations, setting changes or sessions of managed connections. To run several servers at once, set pam-ha: true in guacamole.properties on every server (see the README's High availability section).
PAM_SETTINGS.STANDBY_SHARED_SERVERS: Guacamole servers with the HA module run PAM on this database, so this one, without it, is on standby. PAM is read-only here: no checkouts, approvals, rotations, setting changes or sessions of managed connections. Set pam-ha: true in guacamole.properties on this server too (see the README's High availability section).
PAM_SETTINGS.STANDBY_SERVER_WITHOUT_HA: A Guacamole server without the HA module runs PAM on this database, so this one is on standby until that one stops. PAM is read-only here: no checkouts, approvals, rotations, setting changes or sessions of managed connections. Set pam-ha: true in guacamole.properties on that server too (see the README's High availability section).
PAM_SETTINGS.STANDBY_DATABASE: This Guacamole server cannot reach the PAM database, so it is on standby until it can. PAM is read-only here.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_TEST_SAVE_FIRST: Save your changes first: the test uses the saved settings.
PAM_SETTINGS.INFO_SECRET_SET: Set, encrypted like the other stored secrets; never shown again.
PAM_SETTINGS.SECTION_HELP_SYSLOG: Sends every PAM event to a syslog server (RFC 5424), as it happens on each Guacamole server: rotations, requests and decisions, checkouts, password views, sessions, standby and setting changes. Each message names the event and gives its details as name="value" pairs. Passwords are never sent.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SYSLOG_ENABLED: Off by default. Needs a server below.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SYSLOG_HOST: Host name or address of the syslog server. Over TLS, its certificate must name it.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SYSLOG_PORT: 6514 for TLS; usually 514 over TCP or UDP.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SYSLOG_TRANSPORT: TLS encrypts messages and checks the server's certificate. TCP and UDP send them in the clear; UDP also loses them silently when the server is down.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SYSLOG_CA_CERTIFICATES: For TLS: the certificates, in PEM, of the CAs issuing the syslog server's certificate. If empty, those Java trusts are used.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SYSLOG_FACILITY: The facility of the messages, to route them on the syslog server.
PAM_SETTINGS.HELP_SYSLOG_APP_NAME: What the messages say they come from: "guacamole-pam" if empty. Letters, digits and punctuation, without spaces.
PAM_SETTINGS.INFO_TEST_FAILED: The test could not be sent: {MESSAGE}

PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.HELP_EXPORT: Download the platforms listed, without their passwords, to import them here or on another server.
PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.HELP_RESTORE_DEFAULTS: Add back the default platforms, Unix, macOS and Windows, that are missing.
PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.TEXT_CONFIRM_RESTORE: Add back the default platforms that are missing? Platforms with their names are left as they are, even if changed.
PAM_PLATFORM_TRANSFER.TEXT_NOTHING_RESTORED: Every default platform already exists: {NAMES}. Nothing was changed.

PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.ERROR_NEWER_VERSION: This file was exported by a newer version of the extension.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.ERROR_NOT_PLATFORMS: The provided file must be a platforms export, from the Platforms tab, or a list of platforms.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.ERROR_READ: The provided file could not be read.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_EXISTING: Platforms are matched by name. One that already exists refuses the import unless "Update existing platforms" is ticked. An update cannot change a platform's type, and keeps the passwords it stores when the file leaves them out, unless a setting deciding where they are sent changes (such as its server or port): the file must then give them.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_EXISTING_PLATFORM_MODE: Update existing platforms whose names match those in the file, rather than refusing the import. Passwords left out of the file are kept.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_JSON_DESCRIPTION: A platform import file is what Export writes on the Platforms tab: an object naming its format and version, with a list of platforms. A bare list of platforms is read as well. Each platform has a name, a type (ssh, ldap, kerberos, winrm, tacacs or database), its settings and its rotation policy, and optionally a description.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_JSON_MORE_DETAILS: Settings are named as the platform type names them, such as "script" for SSH, "hostname" for LDAP, "kerberos-realm" for Kerberos or "winrm-port" for WinRM: export a platform of that type to see them. Every platform is checked as when saved in the editor; if any is invalid, nothing is imported, and each invalid platform is listed with why.
PAM_PLATFORM_IMPORT.HELP_PASSWORDS: Exports never contain passwords, which never leave the server. A platform imported may give them among its settings, such as "winrm-admin-password" or "ldap-admin-password". A new platform that needs one is refused without it.

PAM_HA.FEATURE_SHARE_LINKS: Share links of sessions of other servers
PAM_HA.FIELD_GUACD_HOSTNAME: guacd host name for other servers (pam-ha-guacd-hostname)
PAM_HA.HELP_HA: The Guacamole servers sharing this database, as each last reported in. Each server reports every 10 seconds: one not heard from for 45 seconds is no longer counted, and its sessions are removed. Checking the server URLs asks each server running who it is at its URL, with the shared secret, as servers do to fetch recordings from each other.
PAM_HA.WARNING_ALONE: No other server is running: nothing is being shared right now.
PAM_HA.WARNING_LOGINS: Logins are not shared by this server: users log in again when moved to another server. See this server's log for why.
PAM_HA.WARNING_NO_URL: This server sets no pam-ha-url: other servers cannot fetch its recordings, and it cannot be told apart from them but by its host name.
PAM_HA.WARNING_RECORDINGS: Recordings are shown only by the server that has them: set pam-ha-url and pam-ha-secret on every server, or share their recording storage.
PAM_HA.WARNING_VERSIONS: The servers running do not all run the same version of the PAM extension.
